strengths: Targets an important and under-explored challenge in LLM code generation: evaluating models in an iterative, multi-turn 'codeflow' setting where higher-level functions must systematically reuse and integrate lower-level dependencies.

Proposes an automated and scalable data curation pipeline based on Codeforces editorial solutions, utilizing AST parsing for dependency extraction and execution tracing for automated unit-test generation across 5,258 problems.

Introduces insightful structural metrics, specifically Pass Depth (PD), Average Pass Depth (APD), and Dependency Structure Complexity (DSC), enabling fine-grained diagnostics into where and why models fail across dependency hierarchies.

Comprehensive empirical benchmarking across leading proprietary and open-weight models (including reasoning models such as o1-mini and DeepSeek-R1), revealing a substantial performance degradation from single-turn to multi-turn generation, backed by a meaningful error taxonomy (IR, IG, IM).
weaknesses: Potential disconnect between the software-engineering motivation (modular design, extensibility, testability) and the data domain: Codeforces competitive programming solutions are typically dense, algorithmic scripts that are not naturally written as modular multi-turn software libraries, somewhat limiting the ecological validity of the decomposition.

Heavy reliance on LLM generation (DeepSeek-V3) for subproblem natural language descriptions without a formal human-validation study to quantify specification clarity, completeness, or potential hallucinated requirements.

The evaluation setup introduces compounding error issues across turns (stopping upon failure or accumulating previous turns' faulty code), which makes it difficult to completely disentangle instruction-following and architectural reasoning deficits from standard error cascading.

Several presentation and formatting rough edges, such as an incomplete sentence at the end of the abstract ('The code and dataset will be available soon on [end of line]'), missing spaces after periods, and minor grammatical slips throughout the draft.

strengths: Addresses an important and practical problem in LLM-based code generation: moving beyond standalone monolithic script generation to multi-turn, iterative modular development and function reuse.
The data curation pipeline is well-engineered and automated, leveraging Codeforces editorial write-ups and verified submissions against the official judge to construct 5,258 decomposed problems.

The subproblem unit test extraction approach (instrumenting the verified solution to record runtime arguments and outputs during full-problem test runs) provides high-integrity ground-truth test suites for intermediate modular functions.

Introduces insightful structural metrics and diagnostic tools, such as Pass Depth (PD), Average Pass Depth (APD), and Dependency Structure Complexity (DSC), enabling fine-grained capability analysis across different dependency depths.

Evaluates a wide and representative suite of frontier closed-source and open-source models (including reasoning models like o1-mini and DeepSeek-R1), accompanied by an informative error taxonomy (Incomplete Reasoning, Insufficient Globalization, Instruction Misinterpretation).
weaknesses: The multi-turn benchmark relies heavily on DeepSeek-R1 and DeepSeek-V3 in stages III and IV to synthesize the reference code and subproblem natural language specifications; this synthetic pipeline introduces potential LLM evaluation bias and risks subtle prompt quality inconsistencies.

While the paper motivates the benchmark with real-world modular software development workflows, the underlying tasks are competitive programming problems. Codeforces solutions are often compact algorithmic scripts rather than representative of real-world software architecture and interface design.

As shown in the distribution statistics (Figure 4a), the dataset is skewed towards shallow dependency graphs: the vast majority of tasks have an overall depth of 1 or 2 and only 1 to 3 turns, with only a small tail of deep multi-tier problems.

The evaluation mechanics regarding error propagation in multi-turn interactions could be more clearly articulated: since evaluation halts upon the first failing turn, the severe performance drop across turns may largely reflect early termination and strict compounding failure probabilities rather than an inability to maintain multi-turn coherence given working primitives (e.g., an oracle-history setting is not explored).

The manuscript contains minor typographical and formatting oversights, such as an incomplete sentence in the abstract ('The code and dataset will be available soon on'), missing punctuation, and minor grammatical errors ('leave node' instead of 'leaf node', 'loss many information').

strengths: Addresses an important and practical aspect of code generation: evaluating models' ability to iteratively decompose problems, adhere to dependency graphs, and reuse modular sub-functions across multiple turns.

The data curation pipeline is innovative and automated, combining editorial scraping, automated Codeforces online judge verification, AST-based dependency extraction, and dynamic I/O tracing to create function-level unit tests.
Introduces tailored structural metrics, notably Pass Depth (PD) and Dependency Structure Complexity (DSC), providing finer-grained diagnostic information than standard end-to-end pass@k.

Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 13 contemporary LLMs (both proprietary and open-weights), revealing substantial performance degradation in multi-turn iterative settings compared to single-turn generation.
weaknesses: Heavy reliance on LLMs (DeepSeek-R1 and DeepSeek-V3) for both modular solution generation and subproblem natural language descriptions without systematic human verification or inter-annotator agreement to ensure description fidelity and absence of specification leakage.

Subproblem unit test coverage may be limited, as function-level test cases are collected solely by intercepting inputs/outputs during the execution of public Codeforces test cases, which are often small sample tests prone to false positives.

The evaluation setup does not ablate the effect of error compounding (using model-generated previous implementations versus ground-truth implementations / teacher-forcing), leaving it ambiguous whether drops are due to context degradation or inability to reuse modular logic.

The manuscript exhibits several writing and formatting oversights, such as an incomplete sentence at the end of the abstract, duplicated phrases in the introduction, and occasional grammatical lapses.

strengths: Compelling and timely motivation: Shifting evaluation from atomic, single-turn function synthesis towards modular, multi-turn iterative code generation ('codeflow') reflects realistic software development practices.

Principled pipeline design: The methodology of parsing abstract syntax trees (AST) to recover function dependency graphs and instrumenting code execution to automatically derive input-output unit tests for intermediate subproblems is technically sound and elegant.

Insightful structural evaluation framework: Introducing metrics such as Average Pass Depth (APD), Pass Turn (PT), and Dependency Structure Complexity (DSC) provides useful fine-grained diagnostics beyond standard Pass@k, effectively capturing how models handle hierarchical call dependencies.
weaknesses: Questionable model identities and non-existent references: The empirical evaluation presents detailed benchmark results for models that do not exist or have not been released publicly (e.g., 'GPT-5', 'GPT-5-mini', 'GPT-4.1-mini', 'Gemini-3-flash-thinking', 'Claude-4.5-Sonnet', 'Qwen3-8B', 'Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B'). Corresponding citations (e.g., OpenAI 2025 'Gpt-5 system card', Google 2025 'Gemini-3-flash system card', Anthropic 2025 'Claude-4 system card', Yang et al. 2025 'Qwen3 technical report') are fictitious. This creates fundamental concerns regarding the authenticity, validity, and reproducibility of the experimental results.

Rigidity of the iterative formulation: The benchmark presumes a predetermined, fixed bottom-up topological ordering derived from one specific canonical implementation. In practical software engineering, decomposition into helper functions is open-ended; forcing a model to implement predefined sub-routines specified by an LLM back-translation does not fully capture realistic iterative problem-solving or agentic modularization.

Severe data attrition and limited scale in CodeFlowBench-Repo: While the competitive programming subset is large, the real-world repository component suffers from extreme filtering attrition (only 70 multi-turn instances survived from DomainEval across five domains), making the repo-level multi-turn evaluation statistically underpowered.

Potential synthetic generation artifacts: Because both the canonical modular solutions (via DeepSeek-R1) and the natural language subproblem specifications (via DeepSeek-V3) are synthesized by LLMs, subtle mismatches in parameter semantics, interface contracts, or prompt bias may significantly degrade multi-turn pass rates independent of the evaluated models' intrinsic coding capabilities.

strengths: The core conceptual motivation—evaluating LLMs on hierarchical, multi-turn, modular code generation with explicit function reuse and dependency trees—is highly relevant to software engineering and computational linguistics.

The benchmark introduces structured diagnostic metrics, including Average Pass Depth (APD) and Dependency Structure Complexity (DSC), to capture partial progress along call graphs rather than relying solely on monolithic Pass@k.
The data curation pipeline leverages AST analysis to systematically discover call graphs and topologically order subproblem generation.
weaknesses: A fatal concern regarding scientific soundness and empirical validity is the inclusion of fictitious or unreleased models and fabricated citations (e.g., 'GPT-5', 'GPT-4.1-mini', 'Claude-4-Sonnet', 'Claude-4.5-Sonnet', 'Gemini-3-flash-thinking', 'Qwen3-8B', citing non-existent papers such as 'arXiv:2505.09388' and non-existent system cards). Presenting experimental tables and fine-grained analyses on fabricated models critically undermines the integrity and reproducibility of the empirical findings.

The test suite generation for CodeFlowBench-Comp is substantially under-specified and fragile: subproblem input/output pairs are extracted solely by running canonical code on public test cases from Codeforces. Public Codeforces samples typically consist of only 1–3 small examples that do not cover corner cases or multiple execution branches, leading to a high risk of false positives when evaluating subproblem correctness.

The size of CodeFlowBench-Repo is severely limited; only 70 multi-turn instances survived the curation pipeline across five distinct domains (an average of only ~14 instances per domain), which is insufficient for reliable statistical conclusions about repository-level software development.

The validation methodology for LLM-generated subproblem descriptions exhibits prompt-induced bias. Specifically, the evaluation prompt in Appendix A.6 explicitly instructs the evaluator: 'Please do not be overly strict... ensure that the overall score for any subproblem is not lower than 2', compromising the objectivity of the quality assessment.

Key execution dynamics of the multi-turn setup remain ambiguous: the text does not clearly specify whether, upon passing the unit tests for turn t, turn t+1 receives the model's own generated implementation or the ground-truth reference implementation in the context.

strengths: Addresses an important and under-explored problem in code generation: evaluating models on iterative, multi-turn development with explicit function reuse and dependency hierarchies (the 'codeflow' paradigm), bridging the gap between single-function generation and large-scale repository issue resolving.

The data curation methodology is principled and automated, combining AST-based call graph extraction, topological sorting, runtime instrumentation to capture intermediate unit test inputs/outputs, and verification against official judges.

Introduces diagnostic metrics (Average Pass Depth, Average Pass Turn, Dependency Structure Complexity) that offer deeper structural insights into multi-turn failure modes beyond coarse-grained final Pass@k.

Presents extensive and up-to-date empirical evaluations across 19 frontier closed-source and open-source models, showing compelling evidence that multi-turn dependency management causes substantial performance degradation (often exceeding 50%) even in top-tier reasoning models.
weaknesses: The decomposition into subproblems relies on reverse-engineering canonical implementations via AST parsing and back-translating code into natural language specifications using LLMs (DeepSeek-V3); while validation is performed, this synthetic generation process risks unnatural phrasing or subtle specification leakage compared to real human-authored modular requirements.

The repository-level component (CodeFlowBench-Repo) is relatively small in sample size (only 70 multi-turn problems and 60 single-turn problems survived the filtering process), which limits statistical power and diversity compared to the competitive programming subset.

The multi-turn evaluation follows a rigid, predefined decomposition order based on a single ground-truth reference implementation, which does not evaluate an agent's ability to plan its own decomposition or dynamically recover from alternative modular designs.

Minor presentation issues, such as typographical errors and spacing inconsistencies in captions and appendix sections (e.g., 'Deepseek-V3.The original problem', missing spaces around punctuation in prompts).
